messages.content: Write a notice, about 60 words, for the school notice board announcing an inter-house quiz competition.

NOTICE: Inter-House Quiz Competition
An inter-house quiz will be held on Friday, 12 July, at 11 am in the school auditorium. Each house must send a team of three students from Classes 8 to 10. Topics include science, history, sports and general knowledge. Names must be given to the house captains by Tuesday. Come and cheer for your house!
- Quiz Club
Write an invitation, about 60 words, for my daughter Ishita's 7th birthday party. It is on Sunday at 4 pm at Green Park Club, and the theme is jungle animals. It is from Sunita and Prakash.

You are invited!
Ishita is turning seven, and we are having a jungle animals party. Come dressed as your favourite animal and join us for a fun afternoon.
Date: Sunday
Time: 4 pm
Place: Green Park Club
Please let us know if you can join us. We can't wait to see you!
Warm regards,
Sunita and Prakash
Tell everyone in the office, by email, that from Monday, lunch will start at 1 pm instead of 12.30 pm. Keep it to about 40 words.

Subject: New lunch timing

Dear all,
Please note that from Monday, lunch will start at 1 pm instead of 12.30 pm. Kindly plan your day accordingly. If this causes any problem, please let me know. Thank you for your understanding.
Regards
Our family is hosting a Diwali dinner for the cousins on the evening of the festival. Make an invitation for the family group, dinner at 8 pm, 45 words, from Neha.

Dear cousins,
This Diwali, please come to our house for dinner. We will light the lamps together, and dinner will be served at 8 pm. Wear your best clothes and come hungry! It will not feel like a festival without all of you.
Neha
Need a short invitation to my parents' wedding anniversary dinner on Sunday at 8 in the evening. It's a surprise, so mention that. Roughly 35 words, from Anjali.

Please join us this Sunday at 8 pm for a dinner to celebrate my parents' wedding anniversary. It is a surprise, so please do not mention it to them! I can't wait to see their faces.
Anjali
Tell me what a hot bowl of soup tastes like on a cold evening, in 45 words, as a short description.

The soup is thick and golden, and the steam warms my face before I take a sip. It tastes of garlic and gentle pepper, and each spoonful slides down like a small hug. My fingers curl around the warm bowl. The cold evening outside feels far away.
Text for my friend Lucia, about 40 words: her book is back in my bag, I finished it last night, I loved the ending, and I can hand it over when we meet at college on Monday. Sender is Param.

Hi Lucia,
I finished your book last night, and I loved the ending. It is back in my bag now, safe and clean. I can hand it over when we meet at college on Monday. Thank you for lending it to me.
Param
Write today's diary lines from Tomas, about 35 words: he planted tomato seeds in a pot, watered them, put the pot on the balcony where the sun comes in, and is excited to see them grow.

Dear Diary,
Today I planted tomato seeds in a pot. I watered them and put the pot on the balcony, where the sun comes in. Now I must wait, and I am excited to see them grow.
Tomas
Fridge note from Dev for his roommates Hari and Sam, about 35 words: the leftover pasta is for lunch tomorrow, and the cake must not be eaten because it is for a birthday party on Saturday.

Hari and Sam,
The leftover pasta is for lunch tomorrow, so please help yourselves. Please do not eat the cake, because it is for a birthday party on Saturday. Thank you both for leaving it alone.
Dev
A baby shower invitation from the office team for Priya: cake, games, small gifts welcome, in the meeting room at 1 pm. 35 words.
The office team invites you to a baby shower for Priya! It will be held in the meeting room at 1 pm. There will be cake and games, and small gifts are welcome.
Polite complaint to a courier company: my parcel arrived two weeks late and the box was dented, and I want an explanation and an apology. 40 words, signed Lars.

Dear Courier Company,
My parcel arrived two weeks late, and the box was dented. I would like an explanation, and I would also like an apology for the delay and the damage. Please reply to me soon. Thank you.
Lars
A notice for a garden club meeting: the first meeting, bring seeds to swap, in the community garden at 5 pm on Saturday. About 35 words.

NOTICE
The garden club will hold its first meeting in the community garden at 5 pm on Saturday. Please bring seeds to swap with other members. Everyone who loves plants is welcome to join us.
Share a story about a boy and his grandfather on a rainy morning, and use the word umbrella.

The rain would not stop, and Kabir was bored. School was closed, his cricket ball was wet, and his phone had no battery. His grandfather, Dada, looked up from his newspaper.

"Come," he said, taking down an old black umbrella. "I will show you something."

They walked out together, the umbrella drumming over their heads. Dada led him to a small pond, where hundreds of tiny frogs were hopping in the grass. Kabir had never seen so many.

"They only come out when it rains like this," said Dada. "Most people miss them."

Kabir crouched down and watched. His shoes were soaked, and he did not mind at all. On the walk home he asked if they could come again tomorrow.
An old gardener's flowers keep getting dug up by a stray cat. Story, please.

Mr. Pereira had spent twenty years growing roses, and every morning a grey cat dug in the middle of his best bed. He chased her away with a broom. He put wire around the roses. He sprinkled pepper.

The cat kept coming back.

One day Mr. Pereira stayed and watched. The cat scraped out a soft hollow in the cool earth under the biggest bush. Then she went to the hedge and came back carrying a tiny kitten in her mouth. She fetched another, and another, until three kittens lay curled in the shade.

The old man put down his broom.

That afternoon he set an old basket lined with a towel by the wall, under the jasmine. The next morning, the cat and her kittens were sleeping in it, and the roses were left alone.
Young monkey, tall trees, learning to swing: write that story.

Chiku the young monkey sat on a low branch and watched his cousins leap from tree to tree. They shrieked with joy and never fell.

"Your turn," said his Aunt Bandari.

Chiku gripped the branch. The next tree seemed very far. He took a deep breath, swung once, twice, and let go. His fingers missed. He tumbled down through leaves and landed in a soft bush.

He was not hurt, only embarrassed. The cousins laughed, but Aunt Bandari said, "Again."

He climbed back up. This time, he swung harder, reached longer and caught the branch with both hands.

He hung there, swinging, grinning from ear to ear. By evening, he was racing the others through the canopy, shrieking louder than all of them.
Tell me a story about a new student who is afraid to speak in class.

Meera joined Class 5 in the middle of July, and for three days she said nothing at all. When the teacher, Mrs. Pillai, asked her to read aloud, her voice shrank to a whisper and the back benches giggled. Meera went home and told her mother she wanted to leave. The next morning a boy named Jacob slid his notebook across the desk. On the page he had drawn a tiny cartoon of the giggling boys wearing paper hats. Meera laughed out loud before she could stop herself. During reading hour she stood up again, and when the story reached a grumpy old king, she read his lines in a deep, funny voice. This time the whole class laughed with her, and Meera finished the page.
Can you make up a story about a boy who forgets his lines in the school play?

Rohit was playing the king in the Class 6 annual play, and he had practised his speech for two weeks. On the night itself, he stepped onto the stage, saw the rows of parents and felt his mind turn blank. The hall went silent. Behind the curtain, his friend Zoya, who was the queen, whispered the first word. It was not enough. So she walked out, curtsied and said loudly, "My lord, you look troubled. Have the enemy soldiers come again?" Rohit grinned. The line came flooding back and he answered with a thundering speech about the border. The audience clapped so hard that the curtain shook. Afterwards, Zoya asked for a samosa as her payment.
Build a story around a boy and a friend whose model breaks in front of the class.

Edwin and Faiz spent two weeks building a model bridge from ice cream sticks for the Class 8 science test. The day arrived. They carried it carefully to the class, and Edwin set it on the table. The teacher placed a small weight in the middle, and the bridge groaned, then cracked in two. Sticks scattered across the floor. Faiz covered his face. Edwin, though, picked up a stick and examined the break. "Look, the glue failed here, at the joint," he said to the teacher. She raised an eyebrow. "That is a correct observation." They got half the marks for the model and full marks for their explanation, and they rebuilt it that weekend, twice as strong.
Happy ending needed: a story about a farmer whose crops are saved by rain just in time.

Farmer Madhav looked at his dry wheat field every morning and felt his chest tighten. No rain had come for six weeks, and the stalks had turned yellow. His wife, Gauri, prayed at the small shrine each day. One afternoon, a cloud darkened the west, and a cool wind lifted the dust. Madhav ran into the field and stretched out his arms. The first drops fell on his face, then more, and then a steady shower that smelled of earth. Gauri joined him, laughing, in the mud. By evening, the stalks had lifted their heads. The harvest was smaller than usual but enough to feed the village.
Please share a made-up story about two friends who go to the beach for the first time and meet a crab.

Hari and Ameena, both ten, had never seen the sea. When their school bus stopped in Goa, they ran to the shore, shoes in hand. The waves rolled in with a roar and tickled their toes. Ameena laughed and splashed. Hari spotted a tiny crab on the sand, running sideways. "Look!" he shouted. They followed it to a rock pool, where it disappeared under a stone. They crouched and waited, patient. After a long minute, the crab peeked out again and waved a claw. They cheered and dug a small pond for it. At sunset, they said goodbye and promised to come back.
